newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P puts Alcatel, Thomson, Arjil on credit watch.
newsitem.headline: S&P puts Alcatel, Thomson, Arjil on credit watch.

text.p: Rating agency S&P ADEF said it had put under credit watch, with negative outlook, the A-1+ short term note and AA- long-term debt of Alcatel Alsthom and some of its subsidiaries.
It said it had changed to non-defined from negative the outlook for the A- long-term debt of Thomson SA and put the A-2 short-term note under surveillance with non-defined outlook.
The agency also put Banque Arjil, in which Lagardere Groupe has a stake, under credit watch.
Arjil's long-term ADEF A2 note was given a negative outlook while the short term ADEF T1 note was confirmed.
S&P ADEF said in a statement the changes were related to the planned privatisation sales of Thomson SA to either Alcatel Alsthom or Lagardere.
It said its decision followed Alcatel's September 18 news conference during which it gave information about its plans with Thomson if it won the bidding contest.
"The impact of the possible acquisition of Thomson on the credit quality of Alcatel is difficult to estimate at this stage," the rating agency said.
It said the principal uncertainties were the identity of the buyer, the price and method of acquisition, the future legal structure and the implications for the restructuring of Alcatel.
S&P ADEF also said it was as yet unclear where the "considerable debts" currently supported by various entities of the Thomson group would be placed.
The quality of Thomson's portfolio of defence electronics activities and the possibility of partnerships could mitigate the negative effects, it added.
